# Ordinary-result source and checking history

This inert archive preserves 316 original files as 157 content-addressed objects
(843,329 expanded bytes). `first-index.json` binds every original byte and mode;
`first.tar.xz` stores those objects. The passive tests in
`scripts/test_finite_adts_first.py` check the fixed container identities and
links without extracting or executing any saved source or command.

The packet retains the first four desired programs, their actual project and
selected-Raw refusals, separate public-entry repairs, and bounded syntax,
storage and original-root experiments. First failures and later repairs remain
separate. Storage validity alone accepted a valid but incorrectly swapped enum
coordinate mapping; the later actual-root component rejects that map.

The separately observed current CLI packet contains 21 calls. Measured
enum/match/record results, an empty record and a singleton pass project check/run
in text/JSON. Twelve calls succeed; false-pure, quantum-nominal interface and
selected-Raw controls refuse. Independent unnormalized distributions and check
scope fields match. These are informed regression observations, not isolated
first-authoring or general source-preservation evidence. Executable identities
are observations, not native compiler/runtime attestations.

The small Lean component experiments use retained, hash-bound imports and are
not full dependency replays. Both failed attempts to place experimental `#eval`
commands in canonical test sources are retained. The production policy remains
unchanged: generic actual-computation proofs live in the kernel, while maintained
Rust tests invoke the fresh native checker on concrete source/result faults.
Historical experiment commands are never current validation entry points.

General ordinary inputs/functions, selected Raw, quantum nominal owners, full
qmatch and original source/runtime/target preservation remain unfinished.
This archive closes no Issue and admits no guarantee, release or publication.

## Review and complete-input experiments, 2026-10-28

The separate [review archive](review-first.tar.xz),
[index](review-first-index.json) and [summary](review-first-validation.json)
retain four original private-helper/control projects and all eight actual CLI
observations. Called, unused and empty-record private helpers refuse; the
public control succeeds. Originals are never publicized to repair visibility.
Three original active Python consumers and the complete decoded hosted failure
retain the missing result-scope-field expectation; the separate local CLI
reproduction has no separately captured first full streams.

The same passive packet retains a separate complete ordinary-input-family
candidate, its first test-driver syntax mistakes and a formatting-only repair.
All twelve repaired controls pass, including a bad value only at the last
canonical input, erasure of a zero-width argument and an invalid zero-probability
hidden result. A compiled audit covers 373 declarations, including private and
generated helpers, with no project axiom or execution replacement. Generic
proofs connect every canonical input to its actual reconstruction and every
hidden history to typed storage. Retained imports, component proofs and
experiments do not enable a general input runtime or prove source/body/runtime
preservation. Saved commands and modules remain inert; current production
validation and final Issue criteria are separate.

# Ordinary nominal intermediate values in classical bodies

The separate [table-intermediate index](tables-first-index.json),
[inert archive](tables-first.tar.xz) and [validation](tables-first-validation.json)
retain eight informed first projects and sixteen actual pre-change CLI calls.
Four ordinary programs stop at eager finite-table preparation; the built-in
control succeeds, while an actual table consumer, an incomplete unused match
and a false pure effect retain their real refusals. A separate sixteen-call
after capture uses exactly the same source bytes: ten successes and six expected
refusals, with independent result distributions and no source repairs.

The 115 originals / 58 content objects also retain the original committed
consumer, first patch, old-expectation test failure and separate repair. Normal
and MSRV windows remain distinct. Saved commands are never executed; binary
identity, bounded tests and successful checking do not establish source/runtime
preservation, a new guarantee or completed ADT support.

## Zero-width ordinary parameters in closed runtime APIs

The separate [closed-runtime index](closed-runtime-first-index.json.gz),
[inert archive](closed-runtime-first.tar.xz) and
[validation](closed-runtime-first-validation.json) preserve the first selected
prototype's empty-record failure and a separate PR #440-base Rust reproduction.
The latter obtains a real typed native handle for a Unit parameter, then fails
because closed simulation accepts it despite the retained logical argument.
The earlier bounded closedness observations did not cover this case; their
original sources and reports remain unchanged.

The 53 originals / 49 content objects include exact source versions, full
diagnostics and separate repairs. Normal and MSRV each pass nine native
regressions after the repair: Unit, Bits<0>, empty record and nested zero-width
parameters refuse closed simulation/sampling, while a nullary Unit result runs.
The parent Rust checks use the separately observed compatible `8abdf9d` checker;
they are not a fresh checker build for the parent, binary attestation, proof
replay or source/runtime-preservation theorem. Exact candidate CI must build
and test its own checker before merge. Passive history checks never execute
saved sources or commands. No Issue or broader guarantee is completed.
